checked_sources: Frozen REPRODUCE.sh, verify_bitset.py, verify_group.cpp and verify_orbits.py
correctness.rationale: A new standard-library set-based enumeration independently reproduced the full finite finding. It checks the reciprocal degree-four coordinate graph, exhausts the 27 singleton, 351 pair and 2925 triple seeds and updates from the start-of-round observed set; the empty seed plainly cannot observe any vertex. It finds minimum size 3 and 567 triples, with rounds 5:351 and 6:216 and distance types (2,3,3):513 and (3,3,3):54. Enumerating every one-element exchange on that exact state set, with the exchanged vertices adjacent for a slide, yields 5400 and 1242 edges. Full BFS verifies both graphs connected, jump radius/diameter 4/4, slide 7/8 and slide eccentricities 7:432 and 8:135. Its 160461 unordered pairs give the reported 0–5 excess histogram (12501,34830,54189,47250,11340,351) and 54 pairs with distances (1,6); the stated length-six witness is legal and BFS confirms its minimality. Backtracking preserves every mapped adjacency and nonadjacency and considers all unused vertex images, so it enumerates all 54 automorphisms, not only selected generators. Complete group images give the 1 size-27 and 10 size-54 triple orbits, and 3 size-27 and 5 size-54 maximal-penalty pair orbits. The frozen reproduction programs were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Exhaustion applies to the identified coordinate graph, standard synchronous forcing with N[S] at round one, and reconfiguration at exactly the optimum cardinality. It is not a formal proof-assistant certificate.

checked_sources: Compared Pappus exact metric result and general power-domination reconfiguration definitions
value.rationale: Doyle–Holt is a natural small symmetric benchmark, rather than an ad hoc graph picked by numerical outputs. Its sharp example shows that base-graph symmetry and connected minimum-state reconfiguration do not prevent a single unrestricted relocation from requiring six legal local moves. The exact histogram and extremal-pair orbits distinguish coverage delays, connectedness and the number of essentially different geometric bottlenecks; they are useful benchmarks for theory and algorithms for constrained power-domination moves, not merely a recomputation of the graph's order or automorphism count.
residual_risks: It is a finite single-graph classification and does not bound these obstructions on other graphs.
